web_evidence.title: Lolita | Penguin Random House Secondary Education
web_evidence.note: The authorized publisher excerpt spans several opening chapters and repeatedly presents the protagonist-narrator's autobiography as “I,” including “I was born” and “I am writing under observation.”

web_evidence.title: Bouchet, Marie. Focalization and Narration in Lolita, Novel and Film
web_evidence.note: The scholarly abstract describes Humbert as the novel's omnipresent homodiegetic narrator and distinguishes his “narrating I” from his “narrated I.”

web_evidence.title: Orality and Social Memory in Vladimir Nabokov’s Lolita
web_evidence.note: This peer-reviewed analysis says the novel is mostly first-person and explains that apparent third-person or omniscient effects remain rhetorical modes controlled by Humbert, not autonomous narrators.

web_evidence.title: Readers in Pursuit of Popular Justice: Unraveling Conflicting Frameworks in Lolita
web_evidence.note: The thesis identifies the fictional John Ray foreword as a framing voice distinct from Humbert's manuscript; this supports treating the foreword as local framing rather than sustained base-person alternation.

web_evidence.title: Excerpt from Reading Lolita in Tehran by Azar Nafisi
web_evidence.note: The excerpt, reproduced by permission of Random House, places q00705 in Nafisi's memoir and therefore resolves it as foreign to the target novel.

web_evidence.title: rust & stardust in Lolita

person_note: The controlling narrative is Humbert Humbert's retrospective first-person memoir, independently demonstrated by numerous interior quotes, an authorized multi-chapter excerpt, and whole-book scholarly analyses. John Ray's fictional foreword and Nabokov's later afterword are framing paratext, while Humbert's occasional third-person self-reference remains his own controlling voice; neither creates sustained base narration in another person. q00701 is embedded verse, q00705 belongs to another book, and q00719 appears misbucketed upstream. These provenance issues and the few unmarked or gnomic fragments do not create material uncertainty about the FIRST label.
